missing.why: Not missing: Kled himself doesn't die when Skaarl's health empties (label rejected). Expect rejected Guesses.
Chronobreak can save him from lethal damage, but it heals rather than stopping death. Not missing; expect rejected Guesses.
Self-cast Divine Judgment is invulnerability, excluded by the term. Not missing.
Bailout revives an ally only (no self-cast). Not missing.
Comeuppance revives allies only. Not missing.

disputable.why: Lamb's Respite stops everyone dying, enemies too; players may not count it as Kindred cheating death.

aliases.why: The ability text itself spells it this way; check it already normalises.

fun.why: With the Rule no longer naming answers, Sion and Karthus come fast but Kog'Maw, Kindred and Zaahen reward deeper knowledge; small set but satisfying.

champion:Sion.why: Glory in Death is the archetype.

champion:Tryndamere.why: Undying Rage is a first 'can't die' ult for many.

champion:Zac.why: Cell Division is known but second-tier.

champion:KogMaw.why: Icathian Surprise is a known meme, but fewer think of it as cheating death.

champion:Zilean.why: Self-cast Chronoshift is the classic revive.

champion:Kindred.why: Lamb's Respite is known but read as a team ult.

champion:Zaahen.why: Newer champion; his revive is little known.

gemCandidates.why: Icathian Surprise: of course he keeps fighting after dying. Classic 'oh!' reveal that a few players get.
Lamb's Respite keeps Kindred alive too; a fair reveal.
His revive is real but few know it; a fallback.
